title: Block npm Publish
summary: A Claude Code hook that blocks npm publish, pnpm publish and yarn publish in the shell, so shipping a package always stays a human decision.
description: A published package cannot be fully taken back, and the registry keeps the version number forever. This hook watches Bash commands and refuses any publish call from npm, pnpm or yarn.
Dry runs are let through, so the agent can still check what would be packed. Everything else about releases, such as version bumps and changelogs, stays open to the agent.
useWhen: Prepare a release without risking an early publish
Run an agent in a repo that owns a public package
Keep registry tokens from being used by mistake
Let the agent test npm pack but not push the result

hook.command: node -e "let d='';process.stdin.on('data',x=>d+=x).on('end',()=>{let j={};try{j=JSON.parse(d)}catch(e){return}const i=j.tool_input||{};const c=String(i.command||'').replace(/\x22[^\x22]*\x22|\x27[^\x27]*\x27/g,' ')+' ';const t=c.split(/&&|[|][|]|[;|]/).map(s=>s+String.fromCharCode(32));const h=t.find(s=>/^[ ]*(npm|pnpm|yarn)[ ]+(npm[ ]+)?publish[ ]/.test(s)&&!/--dry-run/.test(s));if(h){console.error('Blocked: publishing a package is a human step. Run the build and tests, then ask the user to publish. A dry run (--dry-run) is allowed.');process.exitCode=2}})"

example.prompt: Bump to 2.4.0, run the tests and publish it.
example.result: The version and tests go through. The publish step is refused and the agent tells you the package is ready for you to publish.

faq.question: Can the agent still run npm publish --dry-run?
faq.answer: Yes. A command with the dry-run flag is allowed, so you can inspect the file list that would ship.

faq.question: What about publishing from CI?
faq.answer: This hook only guards the local agent. A CI workflow that publishes on a tag is not affected.

access: Reads each Bash command before it runs
Blocks publish commands and runs nothing itself
